questions.question: What is the exact metrical and rhyme scheme of the nine-line 'Spenserian Stanza' devised by Edmund Spenser for 'The Faerie Queene'?
options: aabbccddee ending with an unrhymed blank line
abbaabbacde ending with a septenary line
ababbcbcc ending with a twelve-syllable alexandrine
ababababcc ending with a decasyllabic couplet
questions.explanation: Spenser added an iambic hexameter alexandrine to eight iambic pentameter lines rhyming ababbcbcc.

questions.question: Sir Philip Sidney's 'An Apology for Poetry' was composed in direct philosophical rebuttal to which anti-theatrical Puritan pamphlet of 1579?
questions.explanation: Stephen Gosson dedicated The School of Abuse to Sidney without permission, attacking poetry as a school of vice.

questions.question: In the prologue to Christopher Marlowe's 'The Jew of Malta', which historical political philosopher speaks the opening lines?
questions.explanation: Machevill introduces the play, declaring I count religion but a childish toy and justifying ruthless ambition.

questions.question: In which exact year and London suburb was Christopher Marlowe fatally stabbed in a room in Eleanor Bull's house by Ingram Frizer?
questions.explanation: Christopher Marlowe died on May 30, 1593 at Deptford, killed following a dispute over the reckoning.

questions.question: Thomas Kyd's 'The Spanish Tragedy' famously opens with a chorus consisting of which two allegorical otherworldly figures?
options: The Ghost of Hamlet's Father and Justice
The Ghost of Don Andrea and Revenge
questions.explanation: The Ghost of Don Andrea and personified Revenge sit on stage as an unearthly chorus overseeing the slaughter.

questions.question: What is the technical rhetorical term for the balanced antitheses, alliteration, and mythical zoology popularized in John Lyly's prose?
questions.explanation: Euphuism was the fashionable high prose style derived from Lyly's Euphues, featuring elaborate parallelism.

questions.question: Which University Wit wrote the delightful romantic comedy 'Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay' alongside the pastoral romance 'Pandosto'?
questions.explanation: Robert Greene wrote Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay, and his romance Pandosto supplied the plot for Shakespeare's Winter's Tale.

questions.question: Which picaresque novel published in 1594 by Thomas Nashe is celebrated as the earliest historical and picaresque fiction in English?
options: The Unfortunate Traveller, or The Life of Jack Wilton
questions.explanation: Nashe's Jack Wilton travels across Renaissance Europe, witnessing wars, Erasmus, and brutal Italian vendettas.

questions.question: Which 1575 work by George Gascoigne represents the first known treatise on English poetic technique and prosody ever printed?
options: Certayne Notes of Instruction concerning the making of verse
questions.explanation: Gascoigne's Certayne Notes provided the earliest practical rules on English accentual meter and word choice.

questions.question: Which Elizabethan critic authored 'A Discourse of English Poetrie' in 1586, urging English poets to abandon rhyme for classical quantitative meters?
questions.explanation: William Webbe praised Spenser while arguing that English poetry should conform to classical Greek and Latin feet.

questions.question: Which 1603 critical treatise did Samuel Daniel compose to defend the natural dignity and musicality of English rhyme against Thomas Campion?
questions.explanation: Samuel Daniel responded to Campion's Observations, arguing that rhyme is natural and suited to modern vernaculars.

questions.question: Who were the two fellow King's Men actors who collected and edited thirty-six of Shakespeare's plays for the First Folio of 1623?
questions.explanation: Heminges and Condell assembled Shakespeare's plays out of love to keep the memory of so worthy a friend alive.

questions.question: Which massive topographical poem in nearly 15,000 alexandrine lines by Michael Drayton provides an exhaustive county-by-county survey of Britain?
questions.explanation: Michael Drayton's Poly-Olbion, published in two parts in 1612 and 1622, is an encyclopedic poetic geography of Britain.

questions.question: What is the title of John Donne's dramatic final sermon preached before King Charles I at Whitehall in February 1631, shortly before his death?
questions.explanation: Donne preached Death's Duel while mortally ill, delivered with such solemnity it was deemed his own funeral sermon.

questions.question: Which emblematic pattern poem by George Herbert was printed vertically in 'The Temple' so that the line lengths visually shape two angelic wings?
questions.explanation: Easter Wings is a visual pattern poem where the expanding and contracting line lengths mirror angelic wings.

questions.question: Which 17th-century devotional metaphysical poet adopted the epithet 'The Silurist' on the title page of his collection 'Silex Scintillans'?
questions.explanation: Henry Vaughan called himself the Silurist after the Silures, an ancient British tribe of his native South Wales.

questions.question: Which metaphysical poet convert to Roman Catholicism authored 'Steps to the Temple' and celebrated Saint Teresa in 'The Flaming Heart'?
questions.explanation: Richard Crashaw's ecstatic baroque verse blends Counter-Reformation mysticism with intense sensory imagery.

questions.question: Which 17th-century metaphysical writer's prose masterpiece 'Centuries of Meditations' remained lost in manuscript until discovered in 1896?
questions.explanation: Thomas Traherne's luminous theological meditations were identified by Bertram Dobell and published in 1908.

questions.question: What title did Robert Herrick give to his immense 1648 royalist collection containing over 1,400 secular and pastoral poems?
questions.explanation: Hesperides, published with his religious Noble Numbers, evokes the golden mythical garden of western poetry.

questions.question: Which Cavalier poet authored the penetrating verse elegy on John Donne, first printed in 1633, praising him for purging English poetry of worn pedantry?
questions.explanation: Thomas Carew's Elegy on Donne famously praises him for opening a fresh, intellectual mine in English poetry.

questions.question: Which 1599 citizen comedy by Thomas Dekker celebrates the rise of the eccentric shoemaker Simon Eyre to Lord Mayor of London?
questions.explanation: Dekker's vibrant comedy dramatises the crafts and apprentices of London with warmth, humor, and civic pride.

questions.question: Which prominent dramatist collaborated with William Shakespeare on late romances including 'The Two Noble Kinsmen' and 'Henry VIII'?
questions.explanation: John Fletcher succeeded Shakespeare as house playwright for the King's Men, co-authoring several late plays.

questions.question: Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher achieved legendary theatrical acclaim by pioneering which mixed dramatic genre for courtly audiences?
questions.explanation: Beaumont and Fletcher perfected tragicomedy in plays like Philaster, bringing characters near death before a happy resolution.

questions.question: In Thomas Middleton's dark Jacobean drama 'The Revenger's Tragedy', what macabre prop does Vindice use to poison the lustful Duke?
options: A poisoned golden chalice at a wedding banquet
A poisoned portrait kissed by the sovereign
An infected letter laced with lethal venom
The poisoned skull of his murdered mistress Gloriana
questions.explanation: Vindice dresses the skull of his dead betrothed in robes and poisons her lips to execute vengeance on the Duke.

questions.question: Which shocking Caroline tragedy of 1633 by John Ford examines the doomed, defiant incestuous passion between Giovanni and his sister Annabella?
questions.explanation: John Ford's masterpiece probes psychological obsession, passion, and moral collapse in Renaissance Parma.

questions.question: Which Jacobean playwright created the grasping, extortionate villain Sir Giles Overreach in the satirical comedy 'A New Way to Pay Old Debts'?
questions.explanation: Philip Massinger's Sir Giles Overreach became one of the most famous, enduring comic stage villains of the period.

questions.question: Which scandalous 1605 stage comedy written jointly by Jonson, Chapman, and Marston led to the authors' imprisonment for anti-Scottish satire?
questions.explanation: King James I was offended by comic gibes about Scottish knights in Eastward Ho, causing the dramatists' arrest.

questions.question: Which landmark court masque of 1605 inaugurated the brilliant theatrical collaboration between Ben Jonson and architect Inigo Jones?
questions.explanation: Commissioned by Queen Anne of Denmark, The Masque of Blackness introduced perspective stagecraft to court.

questions.question: In 'Novum Organum' (1620), Francis Bacon classified the false notions hindering human understanding into four categories called:
options: Shadows of the Past, Present, Reason, and Sense
Idols of the Tribe, Cave, Market, and Theatre
Errors of Scholasticism, Logic, Rhetoric, and Faith
Fantasies of the Body, Mind, Church, and State
questions.explanation: Bacon's doctrine of the Idols exposed deep-seated psychological, linguistic, and philosophical biases.

questions.question: What is the name of the state-sponsored utopian research institute dedicated to natural science in Francis Bacon's 'New Atlantis' (1627)?
options: Salomon's House (The College of the Six Days' Works)
questions.explanation: Salomon's House was Bacon's vision of an organized research college, which inspired the founding of the Royal Society.

questions.question: Which 1658 philosophical prose work by Sir Thomas Browne meditates on human vanity and immortality following the discovery of Roman cinerary urns?
questions.explanation: Browne's Hydriotaphia reflects on mortality, sepulchral rites, and eternity in rich, Latinate prose.

questions.question: Which extensive 1646 scientific and antiquarian treatise by Sir Thomas Browne seeks to refute popular errors, myths, and superstitions?
questions.explanation: Pseudodoxia Epidemica investigated and exploded widespread folklore, superstitions, and natural myths.

questions.question: Which satirical mock-heroic epic poem in octosyllabic couplets was composed by Samuel Butler to pillory puritan hypocrisy during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: Samuel Butler's Hudibras satirises a pedantic Presbyterian knight errant modeled on Don Quixote.

questions.question: Which 1650 political poem by Andrew Marvell adopts a stoic, balanced stance toward the execution of Charles I and the rise of Oliver Cromwell?
options: An Horatian Ode upon Cromwell's Return from Ireland
The First Anniversary of the Government
questions.explanation: Marvell's Horatian Ode famously praises Charles I's royal dignity on the scaffold alongside Cromwell's energy.

questions.question: What is the title of John Milton's 1671 closet drama based on the Greek tragedies of Sophocles and Euripides, depicting the captive Danite hero?
questions.explanation: Samson Agonistes stages blind Samson's patient endurance and catastrophic revenge on the Philistines at Gaza.

questions.question: Which brief four-book epic poem was published alongside 'Samson Agonistes' by John Milton in 1671, centering on the Temptation in the Wilderness?
questions.explanation: Paradise Regained dramatises Christ overcoming Satan's triple temptations in the wilderness through perfect obedience.

questions.question: In March 1649, John Milton was appointed to which official governmental post under the Commonwealth Council of State?
options: Keeper of the State Paper Office
questions.explanation: Milton drafted diplomatic correspondence and official Latin state defenses of the English Commonwealth.

questions.question: Whose 1603 English translation of Michel de Montaigne's 'Essays' provided Shakespeare with the source for Gonzalo's utopian speech in 'The Tempest'?
questions.explanation: John Florio's celebrated translation of Montaigne's Des Cannibales supplied Gonzalo's commonwealth speech in Act II.

questions.question: Which Elizabethan poet and dramatist produced the landmark translation of Homer's 'Iliad' and 'Odyssey' celebrated centuries later by John Keats?
questions.explanation: George Chapman translated Homer into vigorous English verse, celebrated in Keats's famous sonnet.

questions.question: Whose 1579 English translation of Plutarch's 'Lives of the Noble Grecians and Romans' served as Shakespeare's chief source for his Roman tragedies?
questions.explanation: Sir Thomas North translated Plutarch from Jacques Amyot's French version, supplying plots for Julius Caesar and Antony and Cleopatra.

questions.question: What is the popular title of John Foxe's massive 1563 Protestant martyrology, originally titled 'Acts and Monuments'?
questions.explanation: Foxe's Book of Martyrs graphically recorded the trials of Protestant martyrs under Queen Mary I.

questions.question: Which influential 1559 verse anthology edited by William Baldwin featured the ghosts of fallen English statesmen recounting their downfalls?
questions.explanation: A Mirror for Magistrates linked medieval tragedy with Renaissance history, deeply influencing Elizabethan historical drama.

questions.question: In William Shakespeare's 1609 sonnet sequence, sonnets 1 to 126 are predominantly addressed to which aristocratic figure?
questions.explanation: Sonnets 1 to 126 explore themes of time, beauty, procreation, and friendship addressed to a noble young patron.

questions.question: What conventional title is given to the sensuous, dark-complexioned woman addressed in Shakespeare's sonnets 127 through 152?
questions.explanation: The Dark Lady sonnets explore complex, turbulent sexual passion, inconstancy, and psychological torment.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's sonnets 78 through 86, the speaker expresses professional anxiety regarding which mysterious poetic figure?
questions.explanation: The Rival Poet sonnets express anxiety over another poet, commonly identified as George Chapman or Christopher Marlowe.

questions.question: Which elite boys' theatrical company performed indoors at the Blackfriars Theatre, provoking Hamlet's remarks about the eyrie of children?
questions.explanation: The Children of the Chapel were celebrated boy choristers whose popularity rivaled adult professional actors around 1600.

questions.question: What is the full title of Sir Philip Sidney's elaborate prose pastoral romance composed for his sister, published in 1590?
questions.explanation: Sidney wrote Arcadia for his sister Mary Herbert, Countess of Pembroke, blending pastoral romance with statecraft.

questions.question: Mary Sidney, Countess of Pembroke, was one of the foremost literary patronesses of the Renaissance and completed which translation with her brother?
questions.explanation: Mary Sidney completed metrical verse translations of the Psalms begun by Philip Sidney, using over 120 different stanza forms.

questions.question: Which Royalist statesman and advisor to Charles I composed the monumental firsthand historical work 'The History of the Rebellion'?
questions.explanation: Lord Clarendon's History of the Rebellion provides an indispensable, psychologically acute history of the English Civil War.

questions.question: Which historic 1643 military and religious treaty united the English parliamentary forces with the Scottish Covenanters during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: The Solemn League and Covenant secured Scottish military intervention in exchange for reforming the Church along Presbyterian lines.
